title: Digital messages suggesting risk
stem: A client shows farewell messages drafted during a difficult night but never sent. They say they feel embarrassed. Which question best assesses whether the writing reflected preparation for self-harm?
options: Were you preparing to end your life when you wrote these?
Who did you plan to send each of these messages to?
Have you written emotional letters during difficult times before?
Which person on your support list would you like to contact?
why: Directly asking about the purpose of the drafts clarifies possible preparatory behaviour; the answer then informs assessment of current thoughts, intent and safety. Unsent drafts still warrant assessment.
Recipients provide context but do not establish the intent behind writing or present danger.
Past writing habits may inform the history but cannot establish the meaning of this episode.
Support contact can be useful, but current intent should be explored directly rather than inferred from willingness to connect.
takeaway: Assess the meaning of preparatory or farewell communication.
learningObjective: Assess the meaning of preparatory or farewell communication.
